desc:
Workflow logging and audit trail setup gives your automations a memory. Ecom Swift LLC adds a searchable logbook to your workflow that records what came in, what was produced, which rule applied and who approved it.

## What is an audit trail for a workflow?

An audit trail is a time-stamped record of what a workflow did and why. Every run adds an entry: the input it received, the output it produced, the rule or instruction version in use and the person who approved or rejected the result. The log is stored in a sheet or database that you own.

A log differs from a monitoring dashboard. Monitoring tells you whether the workflow is healthy right now. The log tells you what happened on a specific day for a specific customer, long after it happened.

## Why a log matters when questions arrive

Sooner or later someone asks why. A customer wants to know why they received a certain message. A manager wants to know who approved a price change. A supplier disputes an order. Without a record, the answer is a guess, and guesses do not settle disputes.

A log also helps you improve. When an output turns out wrong, you can trace it to the input, the rule and the moment it ran, instead of searching through inboxes and chat threads.

## How logging improves results

Accountability makes teams more careful. When approvals are recorded with a name and a time, reviewers pay closer attention, and gaps in the process become visible. Faster investigation saves hours when something goes wrong, because the evidence is already in one place.

Logs also support better decisions. Filtering entries by date or status shows how often items are held, rejected or fixed, and that tells you which rules to tighten. Whether a log meets any legal requirement depends on your industry and country, so check that with a qualified adviser.

## What a good audit trail includes

- One entry per run, with an exact date and time.
- The input received, or a masked version of it.
- The output the tool produced.
- The rule, instruction or prompt version in use.
- The approver's name and decision, where an approval step exists.
- A status field such as passed, held, rejected or failed.
- Masking for private details such as phone numbers and card references.
- Filters by date, status, workflow and customer.
- A retention period you choose and a way to export records.

## What we do

We identify which workflows need records and what each entry should contain. We then add logging steps to your workflow so that every run writes a row to a sheet or database in your account. We format the log so it is readable by non-technical staff, add filters and test it with real examples.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages add more workflows, approval details, masking, search, retention rules and exports. A short guide explains how to read an entry and how to find a record quickly.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide in advance who may open the log.
- Mask private details unless you truly need them.
- Set a retention period and stick to it.
- Record the version of the rules in use.
- Review a sample of entries every month.

**Avoid:**
- Storing more personal data than the log needs.
- Keeping the log in a shared file that everyone can edit.
- Treating the log as proof of legal compliance by itself.
- Letting entries be changed after the fact.
- Logging so much detail that nobody reads it.

## Who it is for

A business that uses automation for customer messages and wants a clear record of what was sent fits well. A team with approval steps can show who signed off on what. An owner who inherited a workflow built by someone else can add visibility without rebuilding it.

## What we need from you

Tell us which workflows to log and what questions you expect the log to answer. Share the name of the sheet or database tool you prefer, and any rules about private data. We never ask for passwords. We work through a limited collaborator or developer user in your accounts, and the log remains yours.
